video_script.title: William Digby Had 1,100 Pages of Evidence and Nobody in Calcutta Would Read Them
video_script.hook: A British civil servant documented systematic failures during India's 1876-78 famine in two volumes of testimony.
body_slides: William Digby sits in his Madras office. 1878.
His pen moves across testimony after testimony.
The pages pile up. One thousand one hundred.
video_script.voiceover_text: In 1878, a British civil servant compiled 1,100 pages documenting mass starvation in southern India. William Digby's evidence sat unread in Calcutta. The famine killed millions. William Digby sits in his Madras office. 1878. His pen moves across testimony after testimony. The pages pile up. One thousand one hundred. Evidence without audience is just paper. Follow for more stories like this at The Docket.

video_script.hook: New study finds warming signals in 84% of U.S. states when analyzing full temperature distributions.
body_slides: Texas shows no statistical warming signal.
Three hundred died from heat last summer.
The thermometer lies when the system fails.
video_script.voiceover_text: A major study tested every U.S. state for climate warming signals. They found evidence in 84 percent of them. Texas wasn't among them. Texas shows no statistical warming signal. Three hundred died from heat last summer. The thermometer lies when the system fails. Normal doesn't mean safe.
